speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what proportion of courses taken in 2024 with support from SkillsFuture Credits have had direct relevance to the respective individuals' ongoing or future areas of employment; and (b) whether the Ministry has considered introducing conditions for the use of Credits to ensure such relevance, such as requiring courses to be recommended by Government-appointed Skills Development Partners.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: And I have read in the earlier replies over the last few days.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: I have also read the responses to other Parliamentary Questions filed by other Members of Parliament (MPs).

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Many MPs across both sides of the aisle have focused on the utilisation of SkillsFuture Credits and how to increase the utilisation.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: I think we should be asking how SkillsFuture Credits are helping to address the greater economic challenge of this time, which is how it improves the culture of lifelong learning so that it leads to better skills acquisition for better jobs.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: I take the Senior Minister of State's point that the SkillsFuture Credits are first and foremost, meant to improve the culture of lifelong learning.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: To that end, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether the Ministry or the Government has measured the improvement in the culture of lifelong learning and whether it can also measure the translation from that culture of lifelong learning to a culture of skills acquisition that is industry relevant.

And for future tranches of the SkillsFuture credits, would the Senior Minister of State agree that it would be better for our taxpayers' dollars to help encourage Singaporeans to acquire those skills that can help them get good jobs?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The data would suggest it is, if you look at the number of courses, number of training providers and the demand for that type of effort on the supply side.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And there, we do also have to look at some component of utilisation of the SkillsFuture Credit, perhaps as a marker of the take-up of lifelong learning opportunities.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I take his point that that is not the only metric that we should focus on.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do research together with the economic agencies to then make sure that we are achieving the kind of outcomes that he articulated.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Of course, the provision of training through SkillsFuture is not the only thing that then leads to the economic outcomes that he has focused on, but it is something that we have to contribute towards.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We review our policies, we review our programmes to enhance the accessibility, quality and outcomes of our SSG-supported careers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, I thank him for his suggestions and indeed, these are things that we are working towards.
